payload.blocks: Only how pre-approved deviations get approved (DISCUSSION.md §3 rows 6 and 8). The footprint trace, host-step executors, the cleanup rule, the core/debt split and the not-started reason keep shaping without this answer.
payload.headline: Ready plans: when do you approve the answers a plan pre-decides (host steps, named debt, fallbacks)?

parts.cause: Today no per-plan approval by you exists: the planner sets ready after the shape check, the validator's gate auto-approves, the supervisor admits. You approve a discussion when it settles. In the 163-question store, your only overrides of the recommendation were 3 acceptance narrowings (you chose named debt) and 1 standing trust widening, so those are exactly the answers you want to give yourself.

options.cost: Contract text, planning and validating skill text, check rules: about 150-250 lines, no new door.
options.does: You approve the outcome when the discussion settles, with each acceptance criterion marked core or debt-ok. A standing rule pre-approves the fixed classes for every plan (host steps the permission table marks ask, cleanup through the safe door, debt-ok becoming a named backlog row). A plan that needs anything beyond that rule (a new trust boundary, debt on a core criterion) asks you one batched question before it goes ready.
options.gain: No new wait for ordinary plans; you decide the core/debt split where you already decide the outcome.
options.harm: You do not see the exact host argvs of each plan; you rely on the permission table and the rule.
options.label: A. At discussion settle, plus a standing rule

options.cost: Same text and checks plus one question per plan.
options.does: Each plan asks you one batched question showing its unattended-run section; it goes ready only on your answer.
options.gain: You see every pre-decided answer of every plan.
options.harm: Every plan waits for you once (about 30 plans a week), against priority 2.
options.label: B. You approve every plan before ready

options.cost: About the same as A, minus the exception question.
options.does: The planner applies the standing rule and decides the rest itself; you approve nothing new.
options.harm: Plan-specific debt and fallbacks, the place where you overrode before, are never seen by you.
options.label: C. Standing rule only, no approval

parts.recommendation: A. It puts your one decision where you already decide (the discussion outcome), matches your overrides (you chose named debt over re-cuts), and only plans that step outside the rule wait for you.

scope.allows: Shaping the approval moment as answered and writing the standing rule's draft into this discussion.
scope.forbids: Changing any plan, skill or contract now; that waits for the settled discussion and a planner. It does not change the run-time ask rule of ds-jxoz3h2qgk.

parts.what: To let a ready plan run to done without you, the plan would carry its answers in advance: which host steps (full suites, release activation, git recover) the supervisor runs for it, which acceptance criteria may close as named debt, and what to do if a foreseen problem happens. Someone has to approve those answers once, before the run.
